title: Holiday Magic: December Happenings Near Massanutten
seo_title: December Events Near Massanutten | The Valley Edit
subtitle: December Happenings & Local Favorites in the Shenandoah Valley

hero.alt: Snow-covered boulders and bare trees on a Shenandoah ridge as the sun rises over the valley

intro: December in the Shenandoah Valley has a way of slowing everything down in the best possible way. Frost settles on the ridgelines, downtown Harrisonburg glows after dark, and every weekend seems to bring another reason to gather.

From carriage rides and a tree lighting on Court Square to holiday concerts, handmade gifts, and evenings under the lights at Massanutten, this is the month for making traditions, whether they're old favorites or brand new.
Here's what we're looking forward to this December.

items.title: Macbeth at the Forbes Center
items.time: Dec 3–5 at 7:30 PM; Dec 5–6 at 2 PM
items.desc: Shakespeare's darkest drama takes the Mainstage at JMU's Forbes Center for the Performing Arts. A dramatic counterpoint to a month full of tinsel.

items.title: Winter Wonderfest
items.desc: Free horse and carriage rides down Main Street, visits with Santa at the Springhouse on Court Square, a cookie tour, and a gingerbread house competition fill downtown for the afternoon.

items.title: Holiday Parade & Tree Lighting
items.desc: Stay downtown after Winter Wonderfest for the city's "Festival of Lights" parade down Main Street, followed by the tree lighting ceremony in Court Square.

items.title: Ink the Season: Christmas Cards
items.place: Friendly City Clay & Art Center, Harrisonburg
items.desc: An intergenerational card-making workshop for ages 5 and up. Each ticket covers one adult and one child, so it's a sweet way to make something together.

items.title: HolidayFest: Magic and Memories
items.time: Dec 12 at 7:30 PM; Dec 13 at 2 PM
items.desc: The JMU Choral Area and Wind Symphony welcome the season with a festive concert, including music by John Rutter. Tickets are listed at $17–25.

items.title: Last Holiday Market Before Christmas
items.desc: The final Holiday Market of the season, with an expanded lineup of local artisans. Handmade wreaths, jewelry, and gifts are ideal for last-minute shopping.

in_season.title: Saturdays at the Holiday Market
in_season.lead: Skip the mall. December's best gifts are handmade a few miles down the road.
body: For the first three Saturdays of December, the Harrisonburg Farmers Market turns into a Holiday Market, rain, snow, or shine.
Alongside the regular growers and makers, expect an expanded selection of artisan goods: handmade wreaths, herbal self-care, jewelry, and more.
It's an easy morning outing from Massanutten. Grab a coffee downtown, wander Turner Pavilion, and take home a little piece of the valley for everyone on your list.
Still in town after Christmas? A Winter Market follows on Saturday, December 26, from 9 AM–1 PM.

featured.title: An Evening Under the Lights
featured.event: Light Up the Park at Massanutten Resort
body: Some holiday traditions are worth staying in for. This one is worth bundling up for.
Massanutten's Light Up the Park returns on select nights through January 3, with sparkling lights, music, s'mores by the firepit, and Santa appearances on select nights.
Because it's right at the resort, it's an easy addition to an evening at Cedar Escape: dinner at the cabin, a walk under the lights, then home to the hot tub.

Advance tickets are sold online at least one day ahead and cost less than tickets at the door. Kids 2 and under are free. Sessions can sell out, especially on holiday dates, so book early and check the resort's schedule for exact nights.
featured.why: It's the easiest holiday outing of the season. There's no long drive and no packed itinerary, just a magical hour or two a few minutes from the cabin.
featured.close: Go early in the trip, and you may find yourselves going back.

eat.title: A Little Taste of December
eat.lead: Winter Wonderfest is as much about the treats as the twinkle lights.
eat.vendors_intro: On December 5, the downtown Harrisonburg lineup includes:
vendors: The Gingerbread House Gallery at Nest Realty
body: Follow the cookie tour through downtown, stop for a seasonal sip at participating spots, and duck into the gingerbread gallery on West Wolfe Street to admire the competition entries.
Pace yourself and you'll still have room for dinner downtown before the 7 PM parade.
eat.tip: Bring a tote for cookies and gifts, and wear comfortable shoes. Main Street is closed to traffic for the day, so the best way to see it all is on foot.

image.alt: An elaborate gingerbread Victorian house with frosted trees on display among other gingerbread entries
image.caption: Gingerbread house display (file photo)

detour.title: Make Your Holiday Cards by Hand
detour.lead: The cards you send this year could be the ones people keep.
detour.chip: Dec 6 · 12:30–4:30 PM · Ink the Season: Christmas Cards
body: At Friendly City Clay & Art Center in Harrisonburg, creative workshops offer a chance to slow down, try something new, and leave with something you made yourself.
On Sunday, December 6, the studio has scheduled Ink the Season: Christmas Cards, an intergenerational workshop for ages 5 and up, with each ticket covering one adult and one child.
It's a lovely option for families, or for grandparents and grandkids looking for an afternoon together beyond the slopes.
Friendly City Clay is also one of Cedar Escape's local experience partners, with a guest benefit available on eligible scheduled workshops.
detour.note: Workshop availability and discount eligibility should be confirmed before booking.

items.title: PHILADANCO!

items.title: The Magic Flute
items.desc: Mozart's beloved opera comes to the Forbes Center, a perfect excuse for a late-winter weekend in the valley.

ahead.next: Our next edition of The Valley Edit arrives in January with more winter favorites from around the Shenandoah Valley.

closing.title: Make Room for More Memories
body: The holidays are better with room to spread out.
After a day of carriage rides, concerts, and holiday markets, return to Cedar Escape, a spacious five-bedroom retreat inside Massanutten Resort.
Gather for a movie, enjoy the game room, soak in the hot tub, or simply make time to be together.
Because sometimes the best part of a getaway is having nowhere else you need to be.
